reasons: The excerpt presents the commoditized-product-to-undercommunicated-audience repositioning as a blue-ocean marketing strategy and recommends this type of positioning.
This accurately describes the excerpt's greens-powder example, including the stated uncertainty about whether its formula differed.
The listed copywriting elements and the source's stated “at least 70%” result are directly supported by the excerpt.
The recommendation, timing, alternative-solution rationale, and intended outcome are supported.

The asserted depends_on relationship to the broader core-copywriting unit is not stated as a prerequisite in the excerpt; objection handling is introduced as an additional copy element, not as contingent on completing that unit.
The excerpt explicitly critiques the depicted default Shopify-style page as failing the so-what test and leading with features rather than benefits.
The excerpt says free shipping may increase conversion somewhat but argues that its impact is commonly overprioritized, without supplying a numerical estimate.
The excerpt's improved-page example explicitly leads with benefits that pass the so-what test and then explains the mechanism.
The excerpt explicitly says the one-of-one angle is placed up top and describes it as a review-derived specific claim competitors cannot honestly make.
The recommendation to keep cited table-stakes features small and low on the page is supported.

The depends_on relationship to building a benefit-led page is not specified as a prerequisite. The excerpt presents both as components of one example, rather than saying that low placement of table stakes requires the other action.
The excerpt recommends FAQs for purchase-blocking objections, rejects the listed generic FAQ topics, and says the relevant questions are those that might stop conversion.
The excerpt gives a customer-research-based example of identifying key objections and addressing them on the page.
The prerequisite is circular: the action is to use customer research, while the prerequisite already requires that customer research be used to find objections.
The depends_on relationship is also reversed or unsupported: research identifies the objections that an FAQ might answer; the excerpt does not make research dependent on first implementing the FAQ.
The excerpt explicitly distinguishes belief-removing copy from the worth-it question and calls the offer the biggest lever once the latter question arises.
The source does advocate reframing over discounting and says reframing can improve margin through increased average order value.
The exclusion is malformed: “discounting is the wrong frame” is the problem the action addresses, not a circumstance in which reframing should be excluded.
The New Year's-reset example and its stated comparison with sale performance are accurately represented.

The depends_on relationship is unsupported in that direction. The excerpt uses the example to illustrate or support the ensuing reframing recommendation; it does not say the historical example depends on carrying out the recommendation.
The excerpt identifies gifts with purchase and bundles as options that can increase perceived value while preserving or improving margin.
The depends_on relationship to reframing rather than discounting is not established. The excerpt presents gifts and bundles as offer options, not as actions contingent on reframing the product.
This correctly records that the excerpt is cut off before defining the remaining shipping-related lever or completing the statement about what free shipping teaches customers to value.

omissions.description: The critique says generic table-stakes assertions lack proof, beyond merely being feature-led or low-value.
omissions.quote: And anyone can say this. There's no proof that's actually backing it up.

omissions.description: The FAQ example specifically explains a sensitivity-compatible mechanism and answers timing and product-compatibility objections.
omissions.quote: So, we explain the unique mechanism that makes it work on sensitive skin. How long until I see results? Clearly answered here. Can I use it with my other activives? Yes.

omissions.description: The excerpt states a further offer-design objective: reduce cost of goods while increasing customer-perceived value.
omissions.quote: And so we want to decrease our cost of goods while increasing the perceived value from the customer.

omissions.description: The gift-with-purchase example gives a specific implementation: select a high-perceived-value, low-cost gift, offset its cost in pricing, and use full-price anchoring within the bundle.
omissions.quote: So, a gift with purchase, you can put a gift in that might be a product that's valued at $50, but it has a really low cost of goods. It's something like $4. And if you layer that in, you can increase your pricing to offset this $4 cost of goods, but then as a product, the value looks a lot higher because you're discount anchoring at a full price off within the bundle.

omissions.description: The excerpt gives a distinct bundle mechanism: pass shipping and fulfillment efficiency to the customer while increasing units per transaction to raise average order value.
omissions.quote: bundles work really well because they allow you to pass on the shipping and fulfillment efficiency to the customer while pushing up units per transaction, which is one of the biggest levers that underpins average order value.

source_limitations: The excerpt begins mid-sentence and ends mid-sentence, so prior context and the completion of the shipping discussion are unavailable.
The passage appears to be an unedited transcript and contains ambiguous or malformed wording, including “if you just be benefits,” “masterass,” “copyrightiting,” and “activives.”
Claims about conversion, margin, competitive uniqueness, reviews, and offer performance are asserted in the excerpt without underlying data, methods, or corroborating evidence.
The source references separate long-form videos for copywriting and offer curation, but their contents are not supplied here.
